contentBlocks.text: This week you moved from graphing parabolas to solving quadratic equations two different ways. Let's put it all together on one new function.

Quick review: vertex form y=a(x-h)^2+k shows the vertex (h,k) directly (Day 1). Standard form y=ax^2+bx+c requires x=-b/(2a) to find the vertex (Day 2). Factoring solves a quadratic equation using the zero product property when it factors nicely (Day 3). The quadratic formula, x=(-b±√(b^2-4ac))/(2a), solves any quadratic equation, and the discriminant predicts how many real solutions to expect (Day 4). For y = 2x^2 - 4x - 6: find the vertex, then solve 2x^2 - 4x - 6 = 0 using whichever method you prefer (factoring or the quadratic formula), and state which method you chose and why.
Excellent work this week — you can now graph, analyze, and solve quadratic functions using multiple methods, foundational skills for the rest of this Algebra 2 course.

objectives: Find a quadratic function's vertex from standard form
Solve a quadratic equation using either factoring or the quadratic formula, and justify the method chosen
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child find the vertex of y=2x^2-4x-6 independently.
3. Have the child solve 2x^2-4x-6=0, choosing their own method.
4. Complete the cumulative review worksheet.
5. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
6. Celebrate finishing the first full week of Algebra 2 — these methods will reappear constantly throughout the course.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to use the quadratic formula for every equation, even ones that factor nicely, as one consistent reliable method
Ready for more: ask them to solve 2x^2-4x-6=0 using BOTH methods and confirm they give the same answer
This is a good checkpoint to note which part of the quadratic-function chain (graphing, standard-form vertex, factoring, or the formula) needs the most re-teaching
teacherGuide.answerKey: For y=2x^2-4x-6: a=2, b=-4, c=-6. Vertex x-coordinate: -(-4)/(2×2)=1. Vertex y-coordinate: 2(1)^2-4(1)-6=-8. Vertex: (1,-8). Solving 2x^2-4x-6=0: factors to 2(x-3)(x+1)=0, giving x=3 or x=-1 (the quadratic formula gives the same result, since the discriminant is 64, a perfect square).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates Common Core Algebra 2 standards F-IF.7a/F-IF.8a/A-REI.4a-b (graphing, vertex-finding, and solving quadratics via factoring and the formula) before the unit moves to complex numbers and further quadratic applications, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
